programs.Name: The Foundations Trail
programs.pmdm__Description__c:
Foundations Trail is Transition Trails' entry-level 12-week learning program. Learners take on the role of admin for Horizon Community Hub (HCH) — a fictional nonprofit with real problems: grant compliance, case management, data quality, and security architecture. Every week they solve a real business problem by building the actual Salesforce configuration. By Week 12 they have exam-ready knowledge, a working org with 11 complete user stories, an Admin Decision Log, and a portfolio capstone.

Methodology: RESOLVE problem-solving framework
Format: Weekly office hours (Sundays 9 AM CT) + async Build with Me videos + Slack support
Capstone: Horizon Community Hub (HCH) — Administrator Edition
Duration: 12 weeks / 3 sprints (4 weeks each)

Sprint 1 (Weeks 0-4): Foundation — org setup, data model, object manager, security architecture, data management
Sprint 2 (Weeks 5-8): Service Cloud — case management, email-to-case, web-to-case, flow automation
Sprint 3 (Weeks 9-12): Advanced + Capstone — entitlements, escalation flows, dashboards, org handover + Demo Day

Currently in private internal beta with Marissa Pavlak. Beta serves two purposes: (1) help Marissa pass the Administrator exam, and (2) design the program that Penny AI will eventually coach at scale.
programs.pmdm__ShortSummary__c: Entry-level 12-week program for professionals who have earned their Salesforce Platform Foundations credential and are studying for the Platform Administrator certification.
programs.pmdm__TargetPopulation__c: Professionals who have earned the Salesforce Platform Foundations credential but have not yet built anything in Salesforce. They know the concepts but have zero hands-on admin experience. Career pivoters and accidental admins looking to pass the Platform Administrator certification.
programs.Program_Goals__c:
1. Learner passes the Salesforce Platform Administrator certification exam
2. Learner builds a complete working Salesforce org (Horizon Community Hub) with 11 user stories end-to-end
3. Learner produces an Admin Decision Log documenting every configuration choice and business rationale
4. Learner creates a portfolio capstone demonstrating real-world admin skills to employers
5. Beta validates the coaching model and curriculum design spec for Penny AI
programs.Program_Structure__c:
12 weeks / 3 sprints

Week 0: Org Setup & Orientation
Sprint 1 (Weeks 1-4): Foundation - Enhanced Contact Data, Household Account Mapping, Case Privacy & Security Architecture, Federal Funding Eligibility + Data Management
Sprint 2 (Weeks 5-8): Service Cloud - Email-to-Case + Queue Routing, Web-to-Case, Assignment Rules + Auto-Response, Loop Protection Flow
Sprint 3 (Weeks 9-12): Advanced + Capstone - Visual SLA Milestone Tracking, Red Alert Escalation Engine, Donor Impact Dashboard, Org Handover + Capstone Demo Day
programs.Program_Target_Audience__c: Salesforce-certified professionals who have earned the Platform Foundations credential but have never built anything in a real org. They know the concepts but have zero hands-on admin experience. Primarily career pivoters and accidental admins — people who came to Salesforce from operations, support, or business roles and need to prove they can do the work, not just pass a test. Prerequisite: Salesforce Platform Foundations credential.
programs.Program_Expected_Outcomes__c:
1. Learner passes the Salesforce Platform Administrator certification exam

2. Learner completes 11 user stories end-to-end in a working Salesforce org (Horizon Community Hub)

3. Learner produces an Admin Decision Log with 12 documented configuration decisions and business rationale

4. Learner delivers a 5–7 minute Capstone Demo recording suitable for employer portfolio

5. Beta cohort validates the coaching model and curriculum design spec for Penny AI at scale

6. Target: 80%+ story completion rate for primary learner (Marissa Pavlak)

7. Target: Marissa passes the Administrator exam within 60 days of program completion
programs.Problem_Statement__c: Thousands of professionals pass the Salesforce Platform Foundations credential every year and then stall. They have the theory but no hands-on experience, no portfolio, and no proof they can solve real business problems in a live org. Employers won't hire someone who has never actually built anything — and Trailhead alone doesn't fix that. The Foundations Trail exists to close that gap: real problems, real configuration, real proof.
programs.Success_Metrics_Evaluation_Plan__c:
Beta Cohort Metrics (2026):

  • Story completion rate: target 80%+ (Marissa)
  • Office hours attendance rate: tracked via Service Deliveries in Salesforce
  • Admin Decision Log completeness: 12 entries by Week 12
  • Capstone Demo delivered: Yes/No
  • Certification exam passed: Yes/No (tracked post-program)
  • Weekly Jotform feedback score: collected each week, reviewed by Angela

Evaluation Method:

  • Weekly: Jotform feedback form (Form ID: 261306776394061)
  • Monthly: Angela reviews completion rates and adjusts pacing - End of program: Demo Day attendance + cert outcome logged in Salesforce

Post-program:

  • Employment/cert outcome added to Contact record

  • Single beta learner (Marissa) — program validation depends heavily on one person's experience
  • Google Classroom structure incomplete — needs rebuild to match traceability matrix before public launch
  • Penny AI not yet integrated — beta is fully human-coached; Penny design depends on observations from this cohort

Assumptions:

  • Marissa Pavlak completes the full 12-week program
  • Office hours held weekly (Sundays 9 AM CT) with rare exceptions
  • Hugh uploads remaining BWM video content before Marissa reaches those weeks
  • Jotform feedback collected every week without gaps

programs.Name: The Guided Trail
programs.pmdm__Description__c: The Guided Trail is a six-month, project-based internship experience for certified Salesforce Admins. It combines nonprofit consulting projects with structured learning in Transition Trails Academy. Interns work in pods, complete Trail Missions, receive mentoring, and build a live Experience Cloud portfolio.
programs.pmdm__TargetPopulation__c: Individuals who have certifications but not much real world experience.
programs.Program_Goals__c:
By the end of this program, interns will be able to:

  • Apply the R.E.S.O.L.V.E. method to analyze and solve real problems
  • Build secure and scalable Salesforce solutions with best practices
  • Design reports and dashboards that support decision-making
  • Communicate professionally with stakeholders and teammates
  • Work iteratively using Agile ceremonies and tools
  • Present demos and own their narrative through resume and portfolio storytelling

🌍 Our North Star

Every Guided Trail experience should:

  • Empower learners to build and reflect with confidence
  • Connect tools and Trail Missions to real-world use
  • Simulate agile delivery and nonprofit impact
  • Celebrate curiosity, peer learning, and growth

We don’t just teach the tools. We teach the Trail.
programs.Program_Structure__c:
Capstone project - single project each participant must complete

Trail Lessons — Core concepts and frameworks

Trail Missions — Hands-on projects and deliverables

Trail Talks — Weekly coaching or async discussion

Trail Milestones — Uploads and checkpoints for progress

programs.Program_Target_Audience__c:
The Digital Compass Program serves:


  • Small to Mid-Sized Nonprofits: Organizations looking to professionalize their operations and scale their impact.
  • Nonprofit Leaders: Executive Directors, Program Managers, and Board Members seeking specialized knowledge and professional development.
  • Emerging Change-Makers: Community leaders in the early stages of organizational development who need a roadmap for governance and growth.
programs.Program_Expected_Outcomes__c:
3. Core Pillars of Support (The "What")

The program provides structured support and resources across nine foundational areas:


Pillar

Focus Area

Key Deliverables

Strategic Planning

Mission alignment, theory of change, and long-term roadmaps.

Strategic plan templates, quarterly goal-setting workshops.

Board Governance

Fiduciary duties, recruitment, and board/staff relations.

Board handbook templates, governance health checks.

Human Resources

Talent acquisition, retention, and DEI initiatives.

Sample HR policies, compensation benchmarks, and burnout prevention guides.

Volunteer Management

Recruitment, training, and retention strategies.

Volunteer onboarding workflows, management software reviews.

Collaboration & Partnerships

Collective impact and strategic alliances.

Partner mapping tools, MOU templates, and networking mixers.

Fundraising

Grant writing, individual giving, and donor stewardship.

Grant calendars, donor database training, and appeal letter workshops.

Legal & Financial Management

Compliance, budgeting, and risk management.

Internal control checklists, 990 filing guides, and financial dashboard templates.

Technology

Digital transformation, cybersecurity, and CRM systems.

Tech audits, software discounts, and AI implementation guides.

Marketing

Brand storytelling, social media, and public relations.

Editorial calendars, Canva templates, SEO for nonprofits.


4. Program Delivery Model

The community functions through a three-tiered engagement model:


  1. Peer-to-Peer Community: A private digital forum for members to share resources, ask questions, and celebrate wins.
  2. Expert-Led Learning: Monthly "Compass Sessions" (webinars) and deep-dive masterclasses on the nine pillars.
  3. On-Demand Resource Library: A searchable repository of templates, checklists, and recorded sessions.
  4. Project Support: Submitted project work is done pro-bono by participants of our Guided Trail and Trail of Mastery programs.



5. Expected Outcomes & Evaluation

Success will be measured by the following key performance indicators (KPIs):


  • Increased Capacity: 80% of members report improved confidence in at least 3 core pillars within the first 12 months.
  • Organizational Stability: Reduction in leadership turnover and improved financial audit readiness among members.
  • Resource Efficiency: Members report an average of 10+ hours saved per month through the use of program templates and workflows.
  • Collaborative Impact: At least 25% of members engage in a formal partnership or joint venture facilitated by the program.
programs.Problem_Statement__c:
Nonprofits frequently operate in a state of "resource-constrained complexity." While mission-driven, leaders often face significant hurdles in operational management:

• Operational Silos: Expertise in niche areas like legal compliance or digital marketing is often inaccessible due to high consulting costs.
• Leadership Burnout: Executive directors and board members often juggle too many roles without a supportive peer network.
• Knowledge Gaps: Rapid shifts in technology, fundraising trends, and regulatory requirements (e.g., DEI, cybersecurity) create persistent "blind spots."
• Isolation: Small- to mid-sized nonprofits lack the infrastructure for collaborative problem-solving, leading to duplicated efforts and missed opportunities for partnership.
programs.Implementation_Plan__c: Create a Nonprofit Digital Compass digital experience site where nonprofits can register and submit projects

programs.Name: The Trail of Mastery
programs.pmdm__Description__c: The Trail of Mastery is envisioned as an advanced, role-based coaching program designed for professionals seeking to deepen their expertise. Rather than a single-skill course, it will offer distinct paths focused on specific roles, such as Product Owner or Advanced Administrator. The core concept is a cohort model in which teams of participants work on real-world client projects under the direct guidance of an expert coach. This hands-on, project-based approach ensures practical application of advanced concepts. A skills assessment may serve as a prerequisite for entry to ensure participants are prepared for the program's rigor. These product-facing initiatives must be supported by a strong internal operational foundation.
programs.pmdm__TargetPopulation__c:
Primary
Mid-to-senior level professionals who want to move from competent to expert in a specific role

More specifically:

Salesforce Administrators ready to become Advanced Admins / Architects
Business Analysts transitioning into Product Owner roles
Early-stage Product Owners looking to level up into strategic leadership
Technical professionals aiming to gain real-world, client-facing experience

Common characteristics:

3–10+ years of experience
Already certified or formally trained (but lacking depth of application)
Stuck in a “plateau” where learning has become incremental
Wanting credibility, confidence, and proof of capability, not just knowledge

Secondary
Organizations that need stronger, job-ready talent faster

Examples:

Consulting firms (Salesforce partners, implementation teams)
Corporate IT / Product teams
Nonprofits scaling their tech capabilities (aligned with your space)
Training & workforce development organizations

Their pain points:

Talent takes too long to become fully effective
Skill gaps show up in real client/project work
Certifications don’t equal performance
Need a repeatable way to develop high-performing team members

programs.Program_Expected_Outcomes__c:
For Learners:

Participants will demonstrate measurable mastery by successfully delivering real-world solutions, improving competency scores, and advancing into higher-impact roles. These should prove skill mastery, readiness, and confidence in real-world scenarios.

For Organizations:

Organizations will develop job-ready, high-performing talent faster, resulting in improved project outcomes, reduced ramp time, and stronger internal capability.
programs.Problem_Statement__c:
Experienced professionals seeking to advance into specialized roles (e.g., Product Owner, Advanced Administrator) often lack access to structured, hands-on learning that bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and real-world application. Existing training programs are typically either too generic, too passive, or not aligned to role-specific challenges, leaving learners underprepared for complex, client-facing work.

At the same time, organizations struggle to develop talent that can immediately contribute at an advanced level without extensive on-the-job ramp-up. There is a need for a scalable, high-impact learning model that combines role-based skill development, real-world project experience, and expert coaching.
